can_ip_forward.description: Whether to allow sending and receiving of packets with non-matching source or destination IPs. This defaults to false.
can_ip_forward.rationale: Allows non-matching source/destination packets (IP forwarding/spoofing); should stay disabled unless explicitly required (e.g. NAT/router instances).

description.description: A brief description of this resource.

key_revocation_action_type.description: Action to be taken when a customer's encryption key is revoked. Supports "STOP" and "NONE", with "NONE" being the default.
key_revocation_action_type.rationale: Controls whether the instance stops when its CMEK is revoked; default NONE lets the VM keep running on a revoked key, defeating the purpose of revocation.

labels.description:
A set of key/value label pairs to assign to instances created from this template.

				**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
				Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.

machine_type.description: The machine type to create. To create a machine with a custom type (such as extended memory), format the value like custom-VCPUS-MEM_IN_MB like custom-6-20480 for 6 vCPU and 20GB of RAM.

metadata.description: Metadata key/value pairs to make available from within instances created from this template.
metadata.rationale: Free-form key/value store commonly used for security-sensitive toggles (e.g. block-project-ssh-keys, serial-port-enable, enable-oslogin); misconfigured entries weaken instance hardening.

metadata_startup_script.description: An alternative to using the startup-script metadata key, mostly to match the compute_instance resource. This replaces the startup-script metadata key on the created instance and thus the two mechanisms are not allowed to be used simultaneously.
metadata_startup_script.rationale: Arbitrary script executed at boot with root privileges; unreviewed content is a code-injection/backdoor risk.

min_cpu_platform.description: Specifies a minimum CPU platform. Applicable values are the friendly names of CPU platforms, such as Intel Haswell or Intel Skylake.

name.description: The name of the instance template. If you leave this blank, Terraform will auto-generate a unique name.

name_prefix.description: Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with name. Max length is 54 characters. Prefixes with lengths longer than 37 characters will use a shortened UUID that will be more prone to collisions.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

region.description: An instance template is a global resource that is not bound to a zone or a region. However, you can still specify some regional resources in an instance template, which restricts the template to the region where that resource resides. For example, a custom subnetwork resource is tied to a specific region. Defaults to the region of the Provider if no value is given.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

resource_manager_tags.description:
A map of resource manager tags.
				Resource manager tag keys and values have the same definition as resource manager tags.
				Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id}, and values are in the format tagValues/456.
				The field is ignored (both PUT & PATCH) when empty.
resource_manager_tags.rationale: Resource Manager tags can drive tag-based IAM and firewall policy conditions; incorrect tags can unintentionally widen or narrow enforced policy scope.

resource_policies.description: A list of self_links of resource policies to attach to the instance. Currently a max of 1 resource policy is supported.

tags.description: Tags to attach to the instance.

advanced_machine_features.description: Controls for advanced machine-related behavior features.

advanced_machine_features.enable_nested_.description: Whether to enable nested virtualization or not.
advanced_machine_features.enable_nested_.rationale: Nested virtualization increases attack surface and can undermine hypervisor isolation guarantees; should stay disabled unless explicitly required.

advanced_machine_features.enable_uefi_ne.description: Whether to enable UEFI networking or not.

advanced_machine_features.performance_mo.description: The PMU is a hardware component within the CPU core that monitors how the processor runs code. Valid values for the level of PMU are "STANDARD", "ENHANCED", and "ARCHITECTURAL".

advanced_machine_features.threads_per_co.description: The number of threads per physical core. To disable simultaneous multithreading (SMT) set this to 1. If unset, the maximum number of threads supported per core by the underlying processor is assumed.

advanced_machine_features.turbo_mode.description: Turbo frequency mode to use for the instance. Currently supported modes is "ALL_CORE_MAX".

advanced_machine_features.visible_core_c.description: The number of physical cores to expose to an instance. Multiply by the number of threads per core to compute the total number of virtual CPUs to expose to the instance. If unset, the number of cores is inferred from the instance\'s nominal CPU count and the underlying platform\'s SMT width.

confidential_instance_config.description: The Confidential VM config being used by the instance. on_host_maintenance has to be set to TERMINATE or this will fail to create.

confidential_instance_config.confidentia.description:
The confidential computing technology the instance uses.
								SEV is an AMD feature. TDX is an Intel feature. One of the following
								values is required: SEV, SEV_SNP, TDX. If SEV_SNP, min_cpu_platform =
								"AMD Milan" is currently required.
confidential_instance_config.confidentia.rationale: Selects the confidential computing technology (SEV/SEV_SNP/TDX), which determines the strength of the memory-encryption guarantee.

confidential_instance_config.enable_conf.description: Defines whether the instance should have confidential compute enabled. Field will be deprecated in a future release.
confidential_instance_config.enable_conf.rationale: Toggles Confidential VM memory encryption to protect data-in-use; should be enabled for sensitive workloads.

disk.description: Disks to attach to instances created from this template. This can be specified multiple times for multiple disks.

disk.architecture.description: The architecture of the image. Allowed values are ARM64 or X86_64.

disk.auto_delete.description: Whether or not the disk should be auto-deleted. This defaults to true.

disk.boot.description: Indicates that this is a boot disk.

disk.device_name.description: A unique device name that is reflected into the /dev/ tree of a Linux operating system running within the instance. If not specified, the server chooses a default device name to apply to this disk.

disk.disk_name.description: Name of the disk. When not provided, this defaults to the name of the instance.

disk.disk_size_gb.description: The size of the image in gigabytes. If not specified, it will inherit the size of its base image. For SCRATCH disks, the size must be one of 375 or 3000 GB, with a default of 375 GB.

disk.disk_type.description: The Google Compute Engine disk type. Such as "pd-ssd", "local-ssd", "pd-balanced" or "pd-standard".

disk.guest_os_features.description: A list of features to enable on the guest operating system. Applicable only for bootable images.
disk.guest_os_features.rationale: Enables OS-level capabilities (e.g. UEFI_COMPATIBLE, SEV_CAPABLE) required for Shielded VM / Confidential VM support; missing features can silently disable those protections.

disk.interface.description: Specifies the disk interface to use for attaching this disk.

disk.labels.description: A set of key/value label pairs to assign to disks,

disk.mode.description: The mode in which to attach this disk, either READ_WRITE or READ_ONLY. If you are attaching or creating a boot disk, this must read-write mode.

disk.provisioned_iops.description: Indicates how many IOPS to provision for the disk. This sets the number of I/O operations per second that the disk can handle. For more details, see the [Extreme persistent disk documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/extreme-persistent-disk) or the [Hyperdisk documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/hyperdisks) depending on the selected disk_type.

disk.provisioned_throughput.description: Indicates how much throughput to provision for the disk, in MB/s. This sets the amount of data that can be read or written from the disk per second. Values must greater than or equal to 1. For more details, see the [Hyperdisk documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/hyperdisks).

disk.resource_manager_tags.description: A map of resource manager tags. Resource manager tag keys and values have the same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id}, and values are in the format tagValues/456. The field is ignored (both PUT & PATCH) when empty.
disk.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Disk-level Resource Manager tags can drive tag-based IAM/firewall conditions; incorrect tags can unintentionally widen or narrow enforced policy scope.

disk.resource_policies.description: A list (short name or id) of resource policies to attach to this disk. Currently a max of 1 resource policy is supported.

disk.source.description: The name (not self_link) of the disk (such as those managed by google_compute_disk) to attach. ~> Note: Either source or source_image is required when creating a new instance except for when creating a local SSD.

disk.source_image.description: The image from which to initialize this disk. This can be one of: the image's self_link, projects/{project}/global/images/{image}, projects/{project}/global/images/family/{family}, global/images/{image}, global/images/family/{family}, family/{family}, {project}/{family}, {project}/{image}, {family}, or {image}. ~> Note: Either source or source_image is required when creating a new instance except for when creating a local SSD.

disk.source_snapshot.description:
The source snapshot to create this disk. When creating
a new instance, one of initializeParams.sourceSnapshot,
initializeParams.sourceImage, or disks.source is
required except for local SSD.

disk.storage_pool.description: The self_link or ID of the Storage Pool to create this disk in.

disk.type.description: The type of Google Compute Engine disk, can be either "SCRATCH" or "PERSISTENT".

disk.disk_encryption_key.description: Encrypts or decrypts a disk using a customer-supplied encryption key.

disk.disk_encryption_key.kms_key_self_li.description: The self link of the encryption key that is stored in Google Cloud KMS.
disk.disk_encryption_key.kms_key_self_li.rationale: Identifies the CMEK used to encrypt the disk; required for customer-controlled encryption and key revocation.

disk.disk_encryption_key.kms_key_service.description: The service account being used for the encryption request for the given KMS key. If absent, the Compute Engine default service account is used.
disk.disk_encryption_key.kms_key_service.rationale: Determines which service account is used to access the KMS key; defaulting to the Compute Engine default SA is an over-privilege risk.

disk.source_image_encryption_key.description:
The customer-supplied encryption key of the source
image. Required if the source image is protected by a
customer-supplied encryption key.

Instance templates do not store customer-supplied
encryption keys, so you cannot create disks for
instances in a managed instance group if the source
images are encrypted with your own keys.

disk.source_image_encryption_key.kms_key.description:
The self link of the encryption key that is stored in
Google Cloud KMS. Only one of kms_key_self_link, rsa_encrypted_key and raw_key may be set.
disk.source_image_encryption_key.kms_key.rationale: Identifies the KMS-stored key used to decrypt the source image.

disk.source_image_encryption_key.kms_key.description:
The service account being used for the encryption
request for the given KMS key. If absent, the Compute
Engine default service account is used.
disk.source_image_encryption_key.kms_key.rationale: Determines which service account accesses the KMS key; defaulting to the Compute Engine default SA is an over-privilege risk.

disk.source_image_encryption_key.raw_key.description: Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource. Only one of kms_key_self_link, rsa_encrypted_key and raw_key may be set.
disk.source_image_encryption_key.raw_key.rationale: Raw CSEK key material; exposure in config/state would compromise the encryption guarantee.

disk.source_image_encryption_key.rsa_enc.description: Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt this resource. Only one of kms_key_self_link, rsa_encrypted_key and raw_key may be set.
disk.source_image_encryption_key.rsa_enc.rationale: RSA-wrapped CSEK key material; exposure in config/state would compromise the encryption guarantee.

disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.description: The customer-supplied encryption key of the source snapshot.

disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_.description:
The self link of the encryption key that is stored in
Google Cloud KMS. Only one of kms_key_self_link, rsa_encrypted_key and raw_key may be set.
disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_.rationale: Identifies the KMS-stored key used to decrypt the source snapshot.

disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_.description:
The service account being used for the encryption
request for the given KMS key. If absent, the Compute
Engine default service account is used.
disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.kms_.rationale: Determines which service account accesses the KMS key; defaulting to the Compute Engine default SA is an over-privilege risk.

disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.raw_.description: Specifies a 256-bit customer-supplied encryption key, encoded in RFC 4648 base64 to either encrypt or decrypt this resource. Only one of kms_key_self_link, rsa_encrypted_key and raw_key may be set.
disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.raw_.rationale: Raw CSEK key material; exposure in config/state would compromise the encryption guarantee.

disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.rsa_.description: Specifies an RFC 4648 base64 encoded, RSA-wrapped 2048-bit customer-supplied encryption key to either encrypt or decrypt this resource. Only one of kms_key_self_link, rsa_encrypted_key and raw_key may be set.
disk.source_snapshot_encryption_key.rsa_.rationale: RSA-wrapped CSEK key material; exposure in config/state would compromise the encryption guarantee.

guest_accelerator.description: List of the type and count of accelerator cards attached to the instance.

guest_accelerator.count.description: The number of the guest accelerator cards exposed to this instance.

guest_accelerator.type.description: The accelerator type resource to expose to this instance. E.g. nvidia-tesla-k80.

network_interface.description: Networks to attach to instances created from this template. This can be specified multiple times for multiple networks.

network_interface.igmp_query.description: Indicates whether igmp query is enabled on the network interface or not. If enabled, also indicates the version of IGMP supported.

network_interface.network.description: The name or self_link of the network to attach this interface to. Use network attribute for Legacy or Auto subnetted networks and subnetwork for custom subnetted networks.

network_interface.network_attachment.description: The URL of the network attachment that this interface should connect to in the following format: projects/{projectNumber}/regions/{region_name}/networkAttachments/{network_attachment_name}.

network_interface.network_ip.description: The private IP address to assign to the instance. If empty, the address will be automatically assigned.

network_interface.nic_type.description: The type of vNIC to be used on this interface. Possible values:GVNIC, VIRTIO_NET, MRDMA, IRDMA and IDPF

network_interface.queue_count.description: The networking queue count that's specified by users for the network interface. Both Rx and Tx queues will be set to this number. It will be empty if not specified.

network_interface.stack_type.description: The stack type for this network interface to identify whether the IPv6 feature is enabled or not. If not specified, IPV4_ONLY will be used.
network_interface.stack_type.rationale: Determines whether IPv6 is enabled on the interface (IPV4_IPV6/IPV6_ONLY); enabling IPv6 unnecessarily widens the network exposure surface.

network_interface.subnetwork.description: The name of the subnetwork to attach this interface to. The subnetwork must exist in the same region this instance will be created in. Either network or subnetwork must be provided.

network_interface.subnetwork_project.description: The ID of the project in which the subnetwork belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

network_interface.vlan.description: VLAN tag of a dynamic network interface, must be an integer in the range from 2 to 255 inclusively.

network_interface.access_config.description: Access configurations, i.e. IPs via which this instance can be accessed via the Internet. Omit to ensure that the instance is not accessible from the Internet (this means that ssh provisioners will not work unless you are running Terraform can send traffic to the instance's network (e.g. via tunnel or because it is running on another cloud instance on that network). This block can be repeated multiple times.

network_interface.access_config.nat_ip.description: The IP address that will be 1:1 mapped to the instance's network ip. If not given, one will be generated.

network_interface.access_config.network_.description: The networking tier used for configuring this instance template. This field can take the following values: PREMIUM, STANDARD, FIXED_STANDARD. If this field is not specified, it is assumed to be PREMIUM.

network_interface.alias_ip_range.description: An array of alias IP ranges for this network interface. Can only be specified for network interfaces on subnet-mode networks.

network_interface.alias_ip_range.ip_cidr.description: The IP CIDR range represented by this alias IP range. This IP CIDR range must belong to the specified subnetwork and cannot contain IP addresses reserved by system or used by other network interfaces. At the time of writing only a netmask (e.g. /24) may be supplied, with a CIDR format resulting in an API error.

network_interface.alias_ip_range.subnetw.description: The subnetwork secondary range name specifying the secondary range from which to allocate the IP CIDR range for this alias IP range. If left unspecified, the primary range of the subnetwork will be used.

network_interface.ipv6_access_config.description: An array of IPv6 access configurations for this interface. Currently, only one IPv6 access config, DIRECT_IPV6, is supported. If there is no ipv6AccessConfig specified, then this instance will have no external IPv6 Internet access.

network_interface.ipv6_access_config.net.description: The service-level to be provided for IPv6 traffic when the subnet has an external subnet. Only PREMIUM tier is valid for IPv6

network_performance_config.description: Configures network performance settings for the instance. If not specified, the instance will be created with its default network performance configuration.

network_performance_config.total_egress_.description: The egress bandwidth tier to enable. Possible values:TIER_1, DEFAULT

reservation_affinity.description: Specifies the reservations that this instance can consume from.

reservation_affinity.type.description: The type of reservation from which this instance can consume resources.

reservation_affinity.specific_reservatio.description: Specifies the label selector for the reservation to use.

Corresponds to the label key of a reservation resource. To target a SPECIFIC_RESERVATION by name, specify compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name as the key and specify the name of your reservation as the only value.
Corresponds to the label values of a reservation resource.

scheduling.automatic_restart.description: Specifies whether the instance should be automatically restarted if it is terminated by Compute Engine (not terminated by a user). This defaults to true.

scheduling.availability_domain.description: Specifies the availability domain, which this instance should be scheduled on.

scheduling.instance_termination_action.description: Specifies the action GCE should take when SPOT VM is preempted.

scheduling.on_host_maintenance.description: Defines the maintenance behavior for this instance.
scheduling.on_host_maintenance.rationale: Must be TERMINATE (not MIGRATE) for most Confidential VM configurations; an incorrect value can silently break confidential-compute guarantees or fail instance creation.

scheduling.preemptible.description: Allows instance to be preempted. This defaults to false.

scheduling.provisioning_model.description: Whether the instance is spot. If this is set as SPOT.

scheduling.termination_time.description:
Specifies the timestamp, when the instance will be terminated,
in RFC3339 text format. If specified, the instance termination action
will be performed at the termination time.

scheduling.local_ssd_recovery_timeout.description:
Specifies the maximum amount of time a Local Ssd Vm should wait while
  recovery of the Local Ssd state is attempted. Its value should be in
  between 0 and 168 hours with hour granularity and the default value being 1
  hour.

scheduling.local_ssd_recovery_timeout.na.description:
Span of time that's a fraction of a second at nanosecond
resolution. Durations less than one second are represented
with a 0 seconds field and a positive nanos field. Must
be from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.

scheduling.local_ssd_recovery_timeout.se.description:
Span of time at a resolution of a second.
Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.

scheduling.max_run_duration.description: The timeout for new network connections to hosts.

scheduling.max_run_duration.nanos.description:
Span of time that's a fraction of a second at nanosecond
resolution. Durations less than one second are represented
with a 0 seconds field and a positive nanos field. Must
be from 0 to 999,999,999 inclusive.

scheduling.max_run_duration.seconds.description:
Span of time at a resolution of a second.
Must be from 0 to 315,576,000,000 inclusive.

scheduling.node_affinities.description: Specifies node affinities or anti-affinities to determine which sole-tenant nodes your instances and managed instance groups will use as host systems.

scheduling.node_affinities.key.description: Corresponds to the label key of a reservation resource. To target a SPECIFIC_RESERVATION by name, specify compute.googleapis.com/reservation-name as the key and specify the name of your reservation as the only value.

scheduling.node_affinities.values.description: Corresponds to the label values of a reservation resource.

scheduling.on_instance_stop_action.description: Defines the behaviour for instances with the instance_termination_action.

scheduling.on_instance_stop_action.disca.description: If true, the contents of any attached Local SSD disks will be discarded.

service_account.description: Service account to attach to the instance.

service_account.email.description: The service account e-mail address. If not given, the default Google Compute Engine service account is used.
service_account.email.rationale: Determines which service account the instance runs as; falling back to the default Compute Engine SA is an over-privilege risk versus a dedicated least-privilege SA.

service_account.scopes.description: A list of service scopes. Both OAuth2 URLs and gcloud short names are supported. To allow full access to all Cloud APIs, use the cloud-platform scope.
service_account.scopes.rationale: Legacy OAuth scope mechanism. Google's own guidance is to restrict this to ['cloud-platform'] on a dedicated SA and manage granular permissions via IAM roles, since broad legacy scopes bypass IAM-based least privilege.

shielded_instance_config.description: Enable Shielded VM on this instance. Shielded VM provides verifiable integrity to prevent against malware and rootkits. Defaults to disabled. Note: shielded_instance_config can only be used with boot images with shielded vm support.

shielded_instance_config.enable_integrit.description: Compare the most recent boot measurements to the integrity policy baseline and return a pair of pass/fail results depending on whether they match or not. Defaults to true.
shielded_instance_config.enable_integrit.rationale: Detects unauthorized boot-chain modifications by comparing boot measurements to a baseline; defaults to true but can be explicitly disabled.

shielded_instance_config.enable_secure_b.description: Verify the digital signature of all boot components, and halt the boot process if signature verification fails. Defaults to false.
shielded_instance_config.enable_secure_b.rationale: Verifies digital signatures of all boot components and halts boot on failure; defaults to false, so must be explicitly enabled to take effect.

shielded_instance_config.enable_vtpm.description: Use a virtualized trusted platform module, which is a specialized computer chip you can use to encrypt objects like keys and certificates. Defaults to true.
shielded_instance_config.enable_vtpm.rationale: Provides a virtual TPM for secure key/certificate storage and is a prerequisite for integrity monitoring; defaults to true but can be disabled.
